title: Adapted Physical Activity Integrated Into the Care Pathway
official: Integration of Adapted Physical Activity Into the Care Pathway of Patients With Non-small Cell Lung Cancer Treated With Immunotherapy
summary: Lung cancer is the most common cancer across all genders and the leading cause of cancer death. Access to immunotherapy has significantly improved survival for some of these patients. Approximately 20% of patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)), have a prolonged remission lasting beyond two years (long-term lung cancer survivors) which requiring tailored responses in terms of care. Numerous studies have already demonstrated that appropriate physical activity reduces the side effects of cancer treatments and improves patient's quality of life. However, these studies have focused on only certain types of patients. Therefore, investigators wish to examine the feasibility and potential benefice of an integrated approach to adapted physical activity within the existing care pathway for patients with NSCLC in response to immunotherapy treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male, female ≥ 18 years old
* Patient with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer
* Patient receiving immunotherapy for at least 6 months at the time of inclusion
* Disease in response or stable according to RECIST 1.1 criteria at the 6- month assessment at the time of inclusion
* ECOG 0-2
* Affiliated to French health care system, regardless of the regime

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient under legal guardianship
* Patient who is unable to make an informed decision
* Medical contraindication to physical activity
* Pregnant or breastfeeding women
* Persons referred to in Articles L.1121-5 to L.1121-8 of the French Public Health Code will not be eligible for participation in this study.
